ABOUT NYC OUTWARD BOUND SCHOOLS


Founded in 1987, NYC Outward Bound Schools is a nonprofit organization that partners with more than 100 public schools across NYC to engage students in equitable, immersive and joyful learning that prepares them to thrive in community, college and career. Our unique approach to programming focuses on adventurous learning — daring exploration, real\-world engagement, and meaningful challenge — whether in school, local communities, or the outdoors. In schools, we coach teachers and school leaders to implement Crew, our signature advisory structure that supports student connection and belonging, and Instruction for Deeper Learning in the classroom. Outdoors, whether in the city or upstate at our wilderness basecamp, we deliver adventure programming to students, helping them realize that they can do hard things, and develop leadership skills like collaboration and initiative that transfer to the academic classroom. In all spaces where we work, we support students to be co\-creators of their own learning and growth, in environments where their voices are heard and valued. Green Our Planet is a national nonprofit that teaches people to grow food. We run three programs:

**Director of Operations**


New Bedford, MA \| Full time, onsite \| $85,000 to $110,000

**Opportunity**
===============


New Bedford Research \& Robotics (NBRR) is a nonprofit innovation center where advanced technology and creative work happen on a downtown campus. We help entrepreneurs advance new products, run education and workforce programs, and support research. Founders, students, artists, and engineers work in the same rooms and use the same machines.


On any given day you might see a teenager learning industrial robotics, a marine robotics startup testing a vehicle, an artist in residence making a ceramic bowl with a robot, and an engineer refining a new process. Our campus comprises four buildings on “innovation alley” in New Bedford, and will expand from 15,000 to 33,000 square feet this year when we expand our headquarters.


Our home is a legacy site, the old Glaser Glass building, where for many decades people cut and fit glass for this city's cars, houses, and boats. The tools have changed. What happens inside has not: people learning a trade, testing an idea, and finding out whether it works.


This new role is coming at a time of growth at NBRR. We are looking for a person who understands NBRR’s mission and vision, and has the experience and operational leadership skills to scale, balance, and innovate.

**About NBRR**
==============


New Bedford Research \& Robotics’s programs are designed to stand on their own and to make each other better where they overlap:

* Industry R\&D: aerospace, manufacturing, marine tech, architecture and construction, e\-mobility
* Startups in residence: marine robotics, advanced manufacturing, medical, fashion, data, construction
* Research: AI, robotics, design, new materials
* Community: paid internships, a lecture series, artist and designer residencies
* Education and workforce development: marine robotics, industrial robotics, STEAM


NBRR’s staff of engineers, designers, and educators work across all of it, which is how ideas move between a classroom, a startup, and a manufacturer’s research problem.


Today we have seven full\-time staff, two fractional discipline leaders, 20 to 30 interns a year, and a startup membership on track to reach 25 companies in 2027, alongside partner organizations, universities, and schools. Late fall we will open 18,000 square feet of newly fitted out space.

============


This new position will be the senior operating role at NBRR \- focused on orchestrating and systematizing the ecosystem of programs and people that bring our mission to life. Our campus and technology set the stage for NBRR’s team, startups, interns, research partnerships, and community impact. We’re in pursuit of an experienced and vision\-driven person who can maintain balance and contribute to growth across our programs.

**How This Works With the CEO**
===============================


You would report to Mark Parsons, our Founder and CEO. Here is how we see the roles:

* The CEO owns vision and strategy, fundraising, major external relationships, and the board.
* You would own execution and the daily running of the organization: operations, administration, and facilities.
* You would make routine operational, vendor, and personnel decisions within the approved budget.
* You and the CEO will keep a standing cadence to align on priorities, risks, staffing, and what is coming next.
* You would prepare for and present to the Board of Directors at its quarterly meetings.

* Support relationship building with community members and partner organizations, coordinating with the CEO and our organizational leaders.

**Campus**

As a nonprofit organization committed to cultivating an inclusive community environment, we recognize that our greatest strength lies in our people. This position provides high\-level strategic oversight for all fundraising, executive donor relations, board engagement, and development activities. Additionally, the Director champions the organization's mission by directly supporting program operations, including outreach activities, canvassing efforts, and community resource coordination. This is a full\-time position requiring flexible scheduling and occasional evening/weekend availability.

* Develops and implements comprehensive, multi\-year fundraising strategies aligned with the organizational mission.
* Creates annual development plans with specific revenue targets, budgets, and implementation timelines.
* Collaborates closely with the Chief Executive Officer and Board of Directors on organizational fundraising strategy, capital campaigns, and major donor initiatives.
* Analyzes regional and national funding trends to identify new revenue streams and high\-level donor prospects.

**Grant Research and Opportunity Identification** 

* Researches and identifies major grant opportunities from government agencies, national foundations, and corporate funders.
* Oversees the maintenance of a comprehensive grant opportunity database with strict tracking of deadlines and compliance requirements.
* Presents viable grant opportunities to the leadership team with strategic recommendations and ROI analyses.

* Develops annual giving programs, legacy giving initiatives, and specialized donor recognition programs.
* Ensures proper donor acknowledgment frameworks and tax\-compliant gift processing systems are strictly maintained.

**Community Engagement and Partnership Development** 

* Represents Mend Culture Inc. at key community events, networking functions, and fundraising conferences.
* Builds strategic partnerships with civic organizations, faith communities, municipal leaders, and business executives.
* Develops corporate sponsorship programs, workplace giving initiatives, and cause\-marketing partnerships.

* Dental insurance

* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

Chief Operating Officer – Multi\-Location Automotive Repair

**PBAS, LLC is seeking a Chief Operating Officer to lead our automotive repair operations across Tennessee.**

We are looking for a steady, people\-focused leader who enjoys building teams, solving problems, and producing measurable results. The right person wants to win but does not need to dominate the room. They are approachable without avoiding accountability, competitive without creating unnecessary pressure, and organized enough to keep multiple locations moving in the same direction.

The COO will oversee our full\-service automotive repair, exhaust, preventive maintenance, fleet, and USPS vehicle operations. This person will work directly with shop managers, service advisors, technicians, administrative employees, vendors, fleet customers, and ownership.

This is not a desk\-only position. The COO must be visible in the shops, understand what employees need to succeed, recognize problems early, and follow through until they are resolved.

* Identify high\-potential employees and develop future managers and company leaders.
* Create succession plans so individual locations are not dependent on one person.
* Recognize strong performance and provide direct, constructive coaching when improvement is needed.
* Maintain a positive work environment while consistently enforcing company policies and standards.

**ASE Certification and Technical Training**

A major priority of this position will be building a structured ASE certification and technical\-development program.

The COO will:

* Review each technician’s current certifications, skills, and training needs.
* Create individual ASE certification plans with clear goals and timelines.
* Help employees register for ASE testing and obtain appropriate study materials.
* Coordinate training courses, testing schedules, reimbursement, and certification renewals.

* Coordinate specialized training for diagnostics, electrical systems, diesel vehicles, exhaust, fleet maintenance, and emerging vehicle technology.
* Support technical training for Grumman LLVs, Mercedes\-Benz Metris vans, RAM ProMasters, and other fleet and USPS vehicles.
* Build relationships with technical schools and industry training organizations.

**Multi\-Location Shop Operations**

* Oversee daily operations and performance across all PBAS Tennessee locations.
* Visit locations regularly and remain accessible to managers and employees.
* Ensure every shop is clean, safe, organized, properly staffed, and prepared for business.
* Review scheduling, workflow, technician dispatch, bay utilization, parts availability, and vehicle turnaround.
* Identify bottlenecks and correct them before they affect customers or profitability.
* Establish consistent operating procedures while recognizing the different customer and vehicle mix at each location.
* Ensure repairs are completed correctly, documented accurately, and verified before vehicle delivery.
* Review open repair orders, aging vehicles, delayed parts, outstanding approvals, and unfinished work.
* Reduce preventable comebacks and identify patterns involving employees, procedures, parts, vendors, or repair types.
* Ensure managers complete their assigned responsibilities and follow through on company decisions.
* Lead regular management meetings with clear action items, responsible parties, and deadlines.
* Develop and maintain written standard operating procedures for essential shop functions.

Seminole State College of Florida is seeking an accomplished **Executive Director of the Foundation** to lead philanthropic advancement and resource development in support of the College’s mission and strategic priorities.

Reporting to the College President, the Executive Director serves as the Foundation’s chief advancement officer and a member of the College’s executive leadership team. The position provides strategic leadership for fundraising, donor engagement and stewardship, Foundation Board governance, financial management, external relations, and Foundation operations.

The successful candidate will be a relationship\-focused and strategic leader who can build philanthropic support, engage high\-level donors and community partners, work effectively with a Board of Directors, and position the Foundation for long\-term growth and sustainability.

* Develop and execute comprehensive fundraising strategies aligned with the College’s strategic priorities.

**Overview**  

The Regional Managing Director, Data Center Community is an externally facing leadership role responsible for earning and sustaining trust in a major Microsoft data center community or regional cluster of communities. The role serves as Microsoft’s local community leader, local stakeholder point of contact, and chief spokesperson for the assigned region, representing the company with civic leaders, elected officials, business organizations, education and workforce partners, nonprofits, media, and community stakeholders.

  

This position is designed for a high\-visibility data center environment where local trust, transparent communications, public engagement, and community benefit are central to Microsoft’s long\-term license to operate. The Managing Director leads a regional team that includes a Community Manager and a Communications Manager and works in close partnership with the local data center operations, as well as Microsoft legal, government affairs, philanthropic and communications teams to deliver a coordinated, locally empowered, and campaign\-ready approach.

  

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

 **Role Scope and Leadership Model**

* Lead Microsoft’s regional data center community strategy, including local stakeholder engagement, public narrative, community investment, and trust\-building priorities.
* Serve as the chief local spokesperson for the region, shaping Microsoft’s voice in community forums, public events, local media engagements, business and civic convenings, and high\-stakes community conversations.
* Manage and guide a regional team and budget consisting of a Community Manager and a Communications Manager, setting priorities, aligning execution, and ensuring the team operates as one integrated local function.
* Partner closely with the local data center operations leader to align community engagement, communications, and operational priorities, ensuring Microsoft shows up as a coordinated and accountable neighbor.
* Coordinate with regional and national surge teams when new market entry, permitting, zoning, local controversy, media attention, or urgent community concerns require additional support.
* Manage a locally focused budget to enable local partnerships and support community priorities in relation to the data center and its operations.
 **Responsibilities** **Regional Leadership and Community Strategy**

* Own and accountable for the integrated community engagement strategy for the assigned data center region, translating Microsoft’s public Community\-First AI Infrastructure commitments into locally relevant plans, partnerships, communications, and measurable outcomes.
* Build and sustain trusted relationships with local elected officials, civic leaders, business organizations, education and workforce institutions, nonprofits, labor partners, community advocates, and other priority stakeholders.
* Represent Microsoft as a trusted local leader in public forums, community meetings, advisory boards, chambers of commerce, business councils, nonprofit coalitions, and other high\-impact venues.
* Anticipate community risks and opportunities, maintain a clear stakeholder map, identify emerging sentiment, and escalate issues quickly with recommendations for action.
* Ensure community engagement begins early, remains transparent, and continues through the full data center lifecycle, including planning, construction, operations, expansion, and moments of heightened scrutiny.
 **Chief Spokesperson and Public Narrative**

* Serve as Microsoft’s chief local spokesperson for the assigned data center community, delivering clear, credible, plain\-language messages about Microsoft’s investments, operations, community commitments and impact, and long\-term presence.
* Guide the local narrative across community engagement, media, social sentiment, public meetings, and stakeholder communications, ensuring consistency with Microsoft’s regional and national messaging while remaining responsive to local needs.
* Prepare for and lead public\-facing engagements such as town halls, hearings, office hours, tours, groundbreaking events, listening sessions, briefings, and community benefit discussions.
* Work with the Communications Manager to develop talking points, FAQs, briefings, local proof points, media materials, rapid\-response guidance, and storytelling that demonstrates Microsoft’s accountability and community impact.
* Act as the trusted local voice during sensitive moments, helping Microsoft respond with transparency, empathy, speed, and operational accuracy.
 **Communications and Community Engagement Oversight**

* Lead the regional team’s budget communications and community engagement operating rhythm, ensuring the Community Manager and Communications Manager have clear priorities, coordinated plans, and defined accountability.
* Oversee local communications strategy, including proactive storytelling, local media engagement, social sentiment monitoring, stakeholder updates, community event messaging, and crisis\-response readiness.
* Guide community programming and philanthropic investments, ensuring local grants, sponsorships, employee engagement, AI skilling, workforce initiatives, nonprofit partnerships, and education programs align with community priorities and Microsoft commitments.
* Connect communications, media, and community efforts so local programs generate credible proof points and community voices that strengthen trust and demonstrate tangible benefit.
* Ensure the regional team maintains accurate data, metrics, outcomes, and qualitative feedback to support internal reporting, public transparency,

The Director of Operations manages the operational frameworks, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and fiscal metrics of the fitness facility. They lead department heads—including sales, fitness/personal training, front desk, and maintenance teams—to ensure seamless facility performance, brand compliance, and maximum member retention. Marine Corps Community Services (MCCS) is looking for the best and brightest to join our Team! MCCS is a comprehensive program that supports and enhances the quality of life for Marines, their families, and others in the Marine Corps Community. We offer a team oriented environment comprised of military personnel, civilian employees, contractors and volunteers who keep the organization functioning smoothly and effectively. As a service\-oriented organization, we never waver in our commitment to our Corps.
  
  

This position is located at Headquarters, Quantico, VA. Candidates selected for this position will serve as a MCTF Associate Deputy Director NF5\.
  
  

Major Duties
  
  

Serves as the Associate Deputy Director, Marine Corps Total Fitness (MCTF) Directorate, Marine and Family Programs Division (MF), Manpower and Reserve Affairs (M\&RA), Headquarters, United States Marine Corps (HQMC). The incumbent serves as the MCTF Deputy Director¿s full\-time civilian counterpart and second\-in\-command, providing the continuity, technical program expertise, and day\-to\-day operational execution the scope of the portfolio requires. The incumbent independently manages the MCTF portfolio, ensures integration and consistency of policy and execution across all assigned branches, and directly supervises the civilian branch heads for Combat Power Preservation, Outreach and Support, Sexual Assault Prevention and Response (SAPR), and Warrior Athlete Readiness and Resilience (WARR)/Semper Fit. In the Deputy Director¿s absence, the incumbent acts with full authority for the MCTF portfolio, representing the Directorate in Headquarters\-level working groups, budget reviews, and coordination with internal and external stakeholders.
  
  

Serves as the single point of accountability for integration across the MCTF portfolio, ensuring Combat Power Preservation, Outreach and Support, SAPR, and WARR/Semper Fit function as a unified prevention and readiness capability rather than as independent programs. Directs the synchronization of policy, planning, and execution across branches, resolving overlapping mandates, mission gaps, and resourcing conflicts between programs.
  
  

Directs or Leads Operational Planning Teams (OPTs) addressing structural, policy, and governance questions affecting the portfolio.
  
  

Advises the Deputy Director, MCTF on the operational and administrative status of all branches, briefing risks, shortfalls, and resourcing needs in time to support decision\-making.
  
  

Represents MCTF at Department of War and Service\-level meetings, working groups, and boards when the Deputy Director is unavailable, articulating the Directorate¿s position and negotiating solutions that align with strategic objectives.
  
  

Coordinates with other MF divisions, M\&RA staff, and external stakeholders, including Navy and Department of War counterparts, on matters affecting the MCTF portfolio.
  
  

Drafts and reviews policy, decision briefs, and correspondence on behalf of the Deputy Director on portfolio\-wide issues, ensuring alignment with current governing directives and pending policy revisions.
  
  

Exercises full supervisory authority over the civilian branch heads within MCTF. Assigns, plans, and reviews the work of subordinate branch heads, setting priorities and deadlines consistent with MCTF and Division objectives. Evaluates the performance of subordinate branch heads and approves or disapproves leave. Provides input on selection of branch heads, and hears and resolves employee grievances and complaints. Identifies training and development needs and approves training for subordinate staff. Effects minor disciplinary actions and recommends action on more serious disciplinary matters.
  
  

Exercises seasoned analytical ability, judgment, and discretion, applying a thorough knowledge of management principles and program analysis to continuously evaluate the accuracy, effectiveness, and integration of MCTF branch operations. Plans, oversees, and conducts analyses of current and projected programs to identify overlapping mandates, mission gaps, and resourcing conflicts across the portfolio. Analyzes and evaluates data from diverse sources, performing complex qualitative and quantitative analysis. Consults with branch heads, subject matter experts, and representatives of sister services and stakeholder organizations to identify significant factors, relationships, and patterns. Produces interpretive reports and briefs on portfolio operations and integration for the Deputy Director MCTF and other executive\-level personnel, providing options and recommendations for corrective action.
  
  

Develops, coordinates, and submits program requirements and resource needs for assigned MCTF programs and initiatives in support of the Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPBE) process, including Program Objective Memorandum (POM), Current Year Deficiency (CYD), and other budget and resource requirements. **Be a Tar Heel!**
A global higher education leader in innovative teaching, research and public service, the **University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill** consistently ranks as **one of the nation’s top public universities**. Known for its beautiful campus, world\-class medical care, commitment to the arts and top athletic programs, Carolina is an ideal place to teach, work and learn.
One of the best college towns and best places to live in the United States, Chapel Hill has diverse social, cultural, recreation and professional opportunities that span the campus and community.
University employees can choose from a wide range of **professional training opportunities** for career growth, skill development and lifelong learning and enjoy **exclusive perks** for numerous retail, restaurant and performing arts discounts, savings on local child care centers and special rates on select campus events. UNC\-Chapel Hill offers full\-time employees a **comprehensive benefits package**, paid leave, and a variety of health, life and retirement plans and additional programs that support a healthy work/life balance.
  

**Primary Purpose of Organizational Unit**
The Ackland Art Museum is both the best college or university art museum in North Carolina and a very complex organization. With nearly 30 employees, dozens of volunteers, and a budget of approximately $4M per year, the Ackland maintains a collection of over 20,000 works of art. It produces four big exhibitions and many smaller installations annually.  

  

The museum receives nearly 60,000 visitors, always free of charge, who come from all 100 North Carolina counties, across the nation, and internationally each year. The Ackland serves UNC students, faculty, and the public through its special exhibitions, programs, and activities based on its permanent collection. The staff of the Ackland works with approximately 150 faculty and graduate instructors each year to provide opportunities for them to meet their teaching and research goals by bringing their classes to the museum (approximately 10,000 undergraduate, graduate, and professional students). The Ackland provides approximately 20 internships annually for both graduate and undergraduate students. It welcomes and trains a corps of 30 docents to work with K\-12 schools and the public.
  

**Position Summary**
Reporting to the Chief Development Officer and acting as the number two development officer, the Associate Director of Development at the Ackland Art Museum will identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward prospects and donors at the leadership annual giving and major gift level, and create a strategic comprehensive development plan for private support through planned gifts, major gifts, leadership annual giving and corporate and foundation gifts. He/she will assist with staffing board and affinity groups and help plan fundraising and stewardship events, particularly as they relate to leadership annual giving and major gift prospects and donors.  

  

The Associate Director of Development will also participate as a member of the University’s central development organization by attending appropriate campus\-wide development meetings and will occasionally represent the CDO at these and other meetings as appropriate. The Associate Director of Development will serve as a critical partner in expanding development efforts in at the Ackland, including corporation and foundation support, stewardship efforts, donor identification, strategy development, and planning for a building expansion. Overall, the Associate Director of Development will foster collaborative pan\-University development efforts between the Museum and the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. Frequent travel, evening and some weekend work are required.  

  

This position may be eligible for a hybrid work arrangement that may include a partially remote work location, consistent with System Office policy. UNC Chapel Hill employees are generally required to reside within a reasonable commuting distance of their assigned duty station.

Master’s or Bachelor’s and 0\-2 years’ experience; or will accept a combination of related education and experience in substitution.

Strong verbal and written communications skills. Excellent organizational and interpersonal skills and judgment. About Crane Center for Transgender Surgery  


The Crane Center is a world\-renowned Transgender surgical practice, with locations in Greenbrae, California, Boulder, Colorado, and Austin, Texas. We have eight highly specialized surgeons and a multidisciplinary clinical team which allows us to offer all aspects of gender\-affirming surgery.  


We believe in putting the Patient First, and we strive to give employees a work\-life balance that allows the company to recruit and retain the best and the brightest.  


Overview  


Job Title: Chief Operating Officer (COO)  
Reports To: Chief Executive Officer (CEO)  
Department: Executive Leadership  
Job Type: Full\-Time / Executive  


Role Summary  


The Chief Operating Officer (COO) oversees Crane Center’s business development, business operations, administrative services and procedures. The COO will be officed in Austin Texas, however he/she will be responsible for operations and the aforementioned activities at all three of Crane Center locations. As a key member of the executive team, the COO translates the Crane Center’s strategic vision into actionable operational plans that drive growth, expense management and control, quality assurance, patient safety, patient satisfaction, patient communications, office based clinical services, regulatory compliance and medical records , while ensuring sustainable financial performance.  


Key Responsibilities  


Metrics and Target Setting: Partner with the CEO and, as appropriate, other members of the leadership team to develop, monitor and then communicate to the attending staff and clinical and support staff, long term, metrics related to growth, productivity, quality, patient satisfaction and financial performance.  
Alignment: Partner with the CEO and, as appropriate, other members of the leadership team to support the attending physicians in achieving their individual metrics as they relate to growth, productivity, quality and patient satisfaction.  
Cross\-Functional Leadership: Manage and mentor department heads and support staff across core areas including Human Resources, IT, and Marketing to ensure alignment with regards to annual targets and objectives.  
Operational Oversight: Manage daily business operations, optimize internal workflows, and establish policies that promote Crane Center’s operating performance and culture.  
Performance \& Metrics: Monitor performance using Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), delivering timely growth, operational performance, quality reports to the CEO.  
Talent \& Scaling: Partner with the CEO and other members of the leadership team to manage effective recruiting, professional development, and retention strategies to build a stable and high\-performing workforce.  


Qualifications \& Skills  


Experience: 10\+ years of progressive executive leadership experience, with at least 5 years in a senior operational role (e.g. Practice Manager, VP of Operations or COO).  
Education: Bachelor’s degree in Nursing, Other Clinical Sub Spectialty or Business Administration, Finance, Operations Management, or a related field; Master of Business Administration or Health Administration (MBA or MHA) preferred.  
Core Competencies: Strategic planning, financial and operational reporting process optimization, and high\-stakes problem\-solving capabilities.  
Leadership Traits: Outstanding communication, emotional intelligence, resilience, and the ability to cultivate rising talent.
